name: MiniBooNE-DM
summary: MiniBooNE-DM is a dedicated running program within MiniBooNE on the Fermilab Booster Neutrino Beam, Batavia, Illinois. Website statistics should preserve its connection to the parent MiniBooNE experiment.
detection_principle: The proton beam bypasses the normal beryllium target and strikes a downstream steel dump, suppressing conventional neutrinos while retaining dark-particle production. A mineral-oil detector searches for nucleon-, electron- or π⁰-associated scattering.

results.summary: The first dedicated nucleon-scattering analysis found no signal, constraining a sub-GeV vector portal.
Combined nucleon, π⁰ and electron channels improve limits on some light-dark-matter models.

science_scope: Tests dark-sector models by producing candidate particles or portal mediators at accelerators. Invisible accelerator final states or mediator particles alone do not establish cosmic-dark-matter identity; lifetimes, abundance and other experiments must also be considered.
